name: Sanqiao
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 2 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2024. The core lexicon of Sanqiao: a Hmongic language of Guizhou. Paper (23 slides) presented at SEALS 33, Taipei, 15-17 June 2024. academia.edu item 121034570; text of the slides as embedded in the Internet Archive the Internet Archive capture of 2024-06-15 (Glottolog ref 694484).
catalog_locator: slides 'Some phonological features', 'Nature and animal names', 'Other animal names', 'Further dialectal comparisons', 'Sanqiao and data from Li (2000)' (slide deck pp. c. 10-18; the Internet Archive)
catalog_quote: The goal of this presentation is to discuss the classification of Sanqiao, rather than to give a detailed phonology. A detailed phonological description would require more work – eliciting minimal pairs, figuring out tone sandhi, etc. [...] Lexical isogloss: pau 'salt' (with rising tone), in Sanqiao and Caidiwan [...] Sanqiao has lost the final nasal in 'snake' and 'rat' • Like other Qiandong Miao lects, 'snake' and 'rat' are distinguished only by tone [...] 'moon': Sanqiao qa³³li⁵⁵, Ouli li³⁵, Hekou lɛi³⁵, Yuhe ko⁵³qu⁵³ [...] Note that tone categories follow the slashes; phonetic tone values in superscripts precede the slashes

new_statements.relation_note: tonal (contrastive lexical tone, values transcribed); tone inventory and sandhi undescribed; no stress statement
new_statements.rule_in_words: Sanqiao has lexically contrastive tone (minimal pair 'snake' vs 'rat' distinguished only by tone; forms cited with Chao tone values, e.g. 33, 55, rising); the number of tones and tone sandhi are explicitly left undescribed; nothing is said about word stress.
new_statements.exceptions: none; author notes tone sandhi not yet worked out
new_statements.identity_note: Data recorded Aug 2019 at Guben 固本乡 town centre, Jinping County (26.44 N, 108.88 E = Glottolog's coordinates for sanq1234); speaker of 'Qiaohua'; this talk is the basis of the Glottolog languoid. Our bibliography lists the SEALS abstract as read (silent) and the deck as 'not obtained'; the deck text (tables not embedded) has been held by the project since 2026-09-19 but was read only for identity.

sources.note: Nothing on stress. States: 'To date, there have never been any linguistic descriptions or word lists published for Sanqiao.' Data = several dozen basic vocabulary items recorded Aug 2019 in Guben Town, Jinping County; classifies Sanqiao as East Hmongic (Central Miao / 苗语中部方言).

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. MSEA Languages website (sites.google.com/site/msealangs), Hmong-Mien pages and Publications page; Zenodo community search 'Sanqiao'.
sources.note: No Sanqiao word list, recording page or paper is posted on the author's site or on Zenodo.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (English) 'Sanqiao language' and Chinese Wikipedia '三锹话' (wikitext, downloaded 2026-09-17).
sources.note: Nothing on Sanqiao phonology; cite only Hsiu 2024, Yu 2017, Deng Gang 2010 (mountain-land ethnography) and Liu Zongyan 2014 (on Suantang, a Sinitic variety, not Sanqiao).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid page 'Sanqiao' (sanq1234) and its two reference records.
